title: Missing Geo Codes
description:
I think geo location matching is awesome feature, as it allows cross referencing of this dataset against census and other cool things. I tried to find some more matches using [Property Search Form](https://beacon.schneidercorp.com/Application.aspx?AppID=165&LayerID=2145&PageTypeID=2&PageID=1104) and found that in certain cases authorities adjust PID somewhat to accommodate new version of the record (at least this is what I understood is happening). 

In couple of instances I was able to match the observations in the dataset to the records using Lot Area, Total Living Area, Year Built and other variables. For that[ Comparables Search Form](https://beacon.schneidercorp.com/Application.aspx?AppID=165&LayerID=2145&PageTypeID=2&PageID=1105) was useful.

Here's a result of my efforts:

title: Mismatching neighborhoods between 'ames_new' and 'make_ames()'
description:
Hi Max (@topepo), there are slightly different names for what appears to be the same neighborhoods between `ames_new` and `make_ames()`.

The column `ames_new$Neighborhood ` contains only two distinct values, namely "Hayden Lake" and "NridgHt". 
These values do not appear in `make_ames()$Neighborhood ` but 'Hayden_Lake' and 'Northridge' do.

This is very minor, but thought you would be interested in knowing.

```r
library(AmesHousing)

ames <- make_ames()

unique(ames_new$Neighborhood)
# [1] "Hayden Lake" "NridgHt" 

unique(ames$Neighborhood)
# Contains columns 'Hayden_Lake' and 'Northridge'.
```

title: New code for MS_SubClass
description:
The `ames_new` raw dataset has an entry equal to `20` instead of the expected `020` in the column **MS_SubClass**. As a consequence, the make_ames.R script doesn't convert that value to a factor:

https://github.com/topepo/AmesHousing/blob/bbf5351626cfa5272a0cb23b154e8dd9d2d75537/R/make_ames.R#L84

One potential solution is to remove leading zeros from the **MS_SubClass** column before recoding its values. Another potential solution is to recode the value `20` as so:

```
'20' = 'One_Story_1946_and_Newer_All_Styles'
```

title: Add original data documentation
description:
Hi and thanks for awesome package. Since you include ames_raw , i think it makes all sense to ship original Data Documentation file either as vignette or as raw txt file for users to understand original name conventions and the context for certain variables. 
https://ww2.amstat.org/publications/jse/v19n3/Decock/DataDocumentation.txt

I found some of the special notes towards the end of the file extremely useful, in particular regarding outliers. They mess up the models quite badly, as we discovered on [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/c/house-prices-advanced-regression-techniques)
